Question 1
A scientific calculator is required to answer the following question.

The displacement (in meters) of a particle moving in a straight line is given by the equation s(t)=t3−t2−15 where t is measured in seconds. Find the velocity after t=3s.

a
 21m/s
b
 27m/s
c
 14m/s
d
 3m/s
e
 19m/s

decision.explanation: Velocity is the derivative of displacement: v(t)=s'(t)=3t^2-2t. Thus v(3)=27-6=21 m/s.

history.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-{t}^{2}-15) \\  & =3{t}^{2}-2t\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the velocity at $t=3\,\text{s},$ we substitute $t=3$ into the velocity function above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(3) & =3(3)^{2}-2(3) \\  & =27-6 \\  & =21\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

history.worked_solution:
First, we determine $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

For the reference angle, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{R} & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{-1}{-1})| \\  & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1)| \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the point $P$ lies in the third quadrant, we add the reference angle to $\pi ,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta  & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the polar coordinates of $P$ are  $(\sqrt{2},\frac{5\pi }{4}).$

Question 4

Given that x2+31(x−2)2(2x+1)=Ax−2+B(x−2)2+C2x+1, where A, B, and C are real constants, determine the value of A⋅B⋅C.

a
 −70
b
 −56
c
 50
d
 64
e

decision.explanation: Clearing denominators gives x²+31=A(x−2)(2x+1)+B(2x+1)+C(x−2)². Setting x=2 gives B=7; setting x=−1/2 gives C=5. Comparing x² coefficients gives 1=2A+C, so A=−2. Therefore ABC=(−2)(7)(5)=−70.

history.worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x-2)^{2}(2x+1)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+31 & =A(x-2)(2x+1)+B(2x+1)+C(x-2)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=-\frac{1}{2}$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+31 & =A(-\frac{1}{2}-2)(2[-\frac{1}{2}]+1)+B(2[-\frac{1}{2}]+1)+C{(-\frac{1}{2}-2)}^{2} \\ \frac{1}{4}+31 & =A(-\frac{5}{2})(-1+1)+B(-1+1)+C(\frac{25}{4}) \\ \frac{125}{4} & =\frac{25C}{4} \\ C & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=2$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{2}+31 & =A(2-2)(2\cdot 2+1)+B(2\cdot 2+1)+C(2-2)^{2} \\ 35 & =5B \\ B & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, letting $x=0$ and using our values for $B$ and $C$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{0}^{2}+31 & =A(0-2)(2\cdot 0+1)+7(2\cdot 0+1)+5(0-2)^{2} \\ 31 & =-2A+7+20 \\ 31 & =-2A+27 \\ 2A & =-4 \\ A & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Hence,

$$
A\cdot B\cdot C=(-2)\cdot 7\cdot 5=-70.
$$

$$
A\cdot B\cdot C=(-2)\cdot 7\cdot 5=-70.
$$

decision.explanation: Each term integrates to one fifth of a logarithm: (1/5)ln|5x+2|+(1/5)ln|5x−2|+C. Combining the logarithms and absorbing C into a positive constant K gives (1/5)ln(K|(5x+2)(5x−2)|).

Let's solve this using the general formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{1}{5x+2}+\frac{1}{5x-2})\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{5x+2}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{5x-2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡|5x+2|+\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡|5x-2|+C \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡|(5x+2)(5x-2)|+\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|(5x+2)(5x-2)|)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we used the laws of logarithms to write the result as a single logarithm.
